analysis.title: TransUnion (TRU): 3Q First Take: Revenue and margins outperform with the full year guide raised
key_insights: GS expects a positive investor reaction to TRU's 3Q26 print: revenue, EBITDA margin and EPS came in above consensus, and full-year revenue and EPS guidance were raised.
3Q revenue was $1,312.5mn, +12.2% y/y reported versus GS 11.5% and FactSet 11.8%. Organic constant currency (OCC) growth was 7.6%, above GS 7.3% but slower than 10.1% in 2Q.
Excluding FICO mortgage royalties, OCC revenue growth was 5.5% y/y. US Markets grew 7% and International 10% on an OCC basis.
US Markets revenue grew 6.8% y/y OCC, below GS 7.8%. Financial Services +10.8%, Emerging Verticals +5.6%, Consumer Interactive -3.0%.

International revenue rose 10.4% y/y OCC versus GS 5.4%, driven by double-digit growth in Latin America and India, mid-to-high single-digit in Africa, Canada and the UK, and low-to-mid single-digit in APAC.

Adjusted EBITDA margin fell 90 bps y/y to 35.4%, in line with GS and consensus. The decline reflects a 40 bps underlying contraction and a 60 bps drag from zero-margin FICO royalty revenue, partly offset by a 10 bps benefit from Mexico.
Full-year 2026 guidance: revenue raised from $5,127-5,162mn to $5,131-5,162mn, OCC growth of 8-9% reiterated (5-6% excluding the FICO mortgage royalty), EPS raised from $4.75-4.83 to $4.81-4.88.
EBITDA margin guidance was maintained at 35.2-35.4%, down 60-80 bps, including flat to +20 bps of underlying expansion.

The company expects US mortgage revenue to grow 28% in 2026 (9% excluding FICO royalties) despite an ~10% decline in mortgage inquiries. FICO mortgage royalties add ~3 ppt to revenue growth and ~80 bps of margin drag at the midpoint.
4Q guidance: revenue $1,264-1,294mn, EBITDA margin 35.6-36.2%, EPS $1.15-1.22. At the midpoints revenue and EPS are below GS and consensus, and margin is below GS (36.0%) but above consensus (35.8%).

Expected call topics: consumer credit trends, the mortgage outlook at higher interest rates, VantageScore 4.0 adoption in mortgages, non-credit solutions performance, and remaining milestones of the tech transformation program.
GS keeps a Neutral rating with a $68 12-month price target, 14.6% below the $79.62 price on 26 Oct 2026.

market_movers.rationale: The target is 11.5x NTM + 1YR EPS of $5.94, a discount to the Info Services peer median of 18.0x for macro-sensitive transaction revenue and fintech and subprime exposure. The stock trades 14.6% above the target.

earnings_insights: 3Q26 revenue reported $1,312.5mn (+12.2% y/y) versus GS estimate $1,304.2mn (+11.5%) and FactSet consensus $1,307.7mn (+11.8%).
3Q26 adjusted EBITDA reported $464.8mn, 35.4% margin, versus GS estimate $461.6mn (35.4%) and FactSet consensus $462.7mn (35.4%).
3Q26 EPS reported $1.25 versus GS estimate $1.20 and FactSet consensus $1.21.

FY26 guidance EPS raised to $4.81-4.88 from $4.75-4.83. Pre-print GS FY26 estimates were $5,148mn revenue, 35.3% EBITDA margin and $4.81 EPS. Pre-print FactSet consensus was $5,160mn, 35.3% and $4.83.
4Q26 guidance midpoints (revenue $1,264-1,294mn, EPS $1.15-1.22) compare with GS revenue estimate $1,288mn and consensus $1,294mn, and GS and consensus EPS estimates of $1.20.

macro_indicators.interpretation: Mortgage inquiry volumes are falling at higher interest rates, yet TRU expects mortgage revenue to grow 28% (9% excluding FICO royalties).

risk_factors: Growth and margin dilution from M&A
